chunks: Al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:

In mistaken killing resembling intentional killing, such as when one is killed with a whip, a stone, or a stick, the diyyah for that is aggravated, and it is one hundred camels: among them forty pregnant camels, between a thaniyyah and a bāzil in its year, thirty hiqqahs, and thirty bint labūns. As for accidental killing, in it there are thirty hiqqahs, thirty bint labūns, twenty bint makhāḍs, and twenty male ibn labūns. The value of each camel in silver is one hundred and twenty dirhams or ten dinars, and in sheep, the value of each one of the camels is twenty sheep.

key_terms.ابْنَةَ لَبُونٍ: a young she-camel in the labūn age category
key_terms.ابْنَةَ مَخَاضٍ: a she-camel in the makhāḍ age category
key_terms.حِقَّةً: a mature she-camel of a specified age category
key_terms.خَلِفَةً: pregnant she-camel included in the diyyah
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood money due for unlawful killing

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for accidental and شبه العمد killing in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal ruling for diyyah in cases of accidental killing and quasi-intentional killing. It distinguishes the two categories by both the manner of killing and the composition of the compensation, and it also gives equivalent valuation in silver, gold, and sheep.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5196 - Al-Naḍr narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (as) say that the Commander of the Faithful (as) said:

"In the case of accidental killing resembling intentional killing (khaṭaʾ shibh Al-Amd), such as when someone is killed with a whip, a stone, or a stick, the blood money (diyyah) is made more severe. It is one hundred camels, among which are forty pregnant camels between the second and fourth year, thirty mature she-camels (hiqqah), and thirty young she-camels (ibnat labun).
For unintentional accidental killing (khaṭaʾ), the blood money is thirty mature she-camels (hiqqah), thirty young she-camels (ibnat labun), twenty one-year-old she-camels (ibnat makhaḍ), and twenty male young camels (ibn labun). The value of each camel in silver is one hundred and twenty dirhams or ten dinars. In sheep, the value of each camel is equivalent to twenty sheep."
